title: research: stop the one-XOR shear carrier on a lossless integer payload
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Negative stop, no new κ. Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

PR #3947 sends `B = X^2 Y^2` to one XOR, `b ^= c`, on a three-bit quotient. Discussion reply 19032401 asks whether any injective payload encoder makes that XOR a legal consumer. It does not.

- `B^2 - I = [[28, 12], [12, 4]]` has integer kernel `{0}`, so the order-2 carrier does not intertwine with `B` on any nonzero invariant address set.
- Identity 4-bit packing takes `(1, 0)` to `(5, 2)` at Hamming distance 2.
- Mod 4 is the largest quotient with `B^2 = I`. Every wiring into the six-bit caller fails. The quotient map itself is two disjoint XORs and does not use the carrier.
- The exact `m`-bit address caller is four additions. Fixed full adders cost `8m+16` XOR, `8m+16` AND and `4m+8` OR. Restoring the consumed source adds `2m` XOR and `2m` stored bits.

This is not a supplier, a group-algebra register, or a multiplication theorem. The separate faithful-word moment test `M(a) < 1` is not redone.

## Task and overlap

Base `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f`, priority revision 6. Card `bit-new-register-model`, scope **changed**: the card asks for a new nonabelian alphabet, and this package prices the payload encoder left open by the existing shear carrier instead of searching a new word.

Ordered open #1166 handoffs, after exclusions, had 12 entries. Item 17 wraps to index `(17-1) mod 12 = 4`, item 5 (comments 19031016 and 19032401). The piece taken is the payload stop, not the moment inequality.

Nearest work: PR #3905 (four-call formal minimum), PR #3937 (commutative obstruction), PR #3947 (one-XOR carrier and the open encoder question). Overlap with those PRs is the predecessor statement; the kernel, wiring exhaustion, two-XOR quotient circuit, and adder bill are new.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sl2z-payload-encoder-stop
```

Expected: `PASS_SL2Z_PAYLOAD_ENCODER_STOP ... wiring_hits=0 mod4_direct_xor=2 ... no_new_kappa=true` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`.

Also passed: metadata pins, `check_research_commit.py` at `900d5b61df7988895c5db95a8c36008f2229c1e8`, and `python3.12 -I -B -O -Werror` on `verify.py` (checks are raises, not stripped asserts).

The wiring search is exhaustive for bit placement and constant scratch. It is not a search over arbitrary circuits. The integer kernel argument is proved in the README and corroborated on `[-12, 12]^2`. No selected cold replay, Lean, or Docker run.

Positive control: the same wiring search accepts the carrier's own XOR as a target. Negative control: three shears do not send `(1, 0)` to `(5, 2)`.

## Credit

PR #3905, 1337isnot1337 / OpenAI Codex. PR #3937 and PR #3947, ToikY / OpenAI Codex, including the payload question in discussion reply 19032401. New checks by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok 4.7 assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Can the low two bits of an exact `m`-bit address use the mod-4 two-XOR map while a carry into the high half replaces one of the four additions? First step: one shear's high-half recurrence on a single `m = 4` witness. Blocked if that carry is itself an addition; the split then does not beat `8m+16` XORs plus the matching ANDs and ORs. See `research/sl2z-payload-encoder-stop/README.md`.
